themes.name: Agentic AI in research
themes.description: Focuses on AI agents that perform research tasks autonomously, including agents for intelligence gathering, workflow automation, and complex problem-solving.

themes.name: AI coding assistants
themes.description: Covers AI tools and research that assist in writing, debugging, and understanding code, often integrated into development workflows.

themes.name: AI research tools
themes.description: Encompasses articles discussing a broad range of AI tools designed to aid researchers in various aspects of their work, from data analysis to literature review.

themes.name: AI summarization
themes.description: Articles focused on AI's ability to condense large amounts of text into concise summaries, useful for reports, meetings, and research synthesis.

themes.name: Synthetic users
themes.description: Explores the creation and use of artificial user profiles or 'digital twins' for testing, data generation, and market research simulations.

themes.name: AI-powered data analysis
themes.description: Details how AI is used to analyze qualitative and quantitative data, uncovering insights, identifying patterns, and driving decision-making.

themes.name: AI chatbot research
themes.description: Investigates the use of AI chatbots in research contexts, including their impact on user trust, learning, and the potential for misinformation.

themes.name: AI workforce impact
themes.description: Examines how AI is affecting jobs, skills, and employment trends, including concerns about job displacement and the need for reskilling.

themes.name: AI for design & research
themes.description: Focuses on AI's application in the creative process for design and research, including AI-assisted ideation, prototyping, and workflow optimization.

themes.name: AI testing automation
themes.description: Covers the application of AI in automating software testing processes, including functional, accessibility, and performance testing.

note: Themes identified by analyzing articles from curated sources, Google News, HackerNews, and DEV.to this month.
